messages:
eli: hey team, first day — trying to build the runtime from source and hitting a weird Thrust/CUDA link error. any quick pointers?

eli: error snippet:
```
/usr/bin/ld: CMakeFiles/runtime.dir/src/gpu/kv_cache.o: in function `anonymous namespace'...'
/usr/bin/ld: /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so: undefined reference to `__cudaRegisterFatBinary'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

eli: i'm on Ubuntu 22.04, CUDA 12.1 (installed from deb), driver 535.54, gcc 11.3.0. cmake picks up /usr/local/cuda.

mika: welcome eli! :wave: first guess is mixed CUDA toolkit vs driver vs packaged cudart. can you paste output of `nvcc --version` and `nvidia-smi`? also `ls -l /usr/local/cuda`?

eli: nvcc --version:
```
nvcc: NVIDIA (R) Cuda compiler driver
Cuda compilation tools, release 12.1, V12.1.105
```

eli: nvidia-smi:
```
NVIDIA-SMI 535.54       Driver Version: 535.54       CUDA Version: 12.1
```

rosie: do you have any cuda libs installed from apt simultaneously? sometimes distro packages (libcudart from apt) conflict with the toolkit in /usr/local/cuda. `ldd` on the binary or object file can show which libcudart is being linked.

eli: good call — `ldd build/bin/runtime` shows libcudart.so.12 -> /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcudart.so.12 (from apt) not /usr/local/cuda.

samir: that mismatch is your culprit. two ways: 1) point CMAKE to the toolkit explicitly with `-DCUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR=/usr/local/cuda-12.1` and update LD_LIBRARY_PATH to prefer /usr/local/cuda/lib64, or 2) remove the distro cuda runtime package.

mika: additionally if you built with a different libstdc++ or ABI, you'll see __cxx11 symbols. make sure your gcc matches the dev container/toolchain used by the repo. we usually use gcc-11 on dev machines.

eli: tried `export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH` and re-linked, but still get undefined ref to cublas symbols during link: `undefined reference to cublasCreate_v2`

rosie: is libcublas present in /usr/local/cuda/lib64? `ls /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcublas*`

eli: `ls` shows libcublas.so -> /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcublas.so.12 (again apt). weird.

buildbot: CI image note: the official dev image we recommend is `redwood/dev-runtime:2025-03` which has CUDA toolkit and libs aligned. see https://ci.redwood.com/dev-images/runtime for tips.

samir: if apt-installed runtime libs are taking precedence, a quick workaround is creating a local symlink to the toolkit libs in a folder and using `LD_PRELOAD` or adding that folder to `/etc/ld.so.conf.d/` with `ldconfig` so the loader prefers /usr/local/cuda. but long-term fix: uninstall the system cuda packages.

eli: can i safely remove `nvidia-cuda-toolkit` and `libcudart-12-1`? or will that break other apps?

mika: safe on your dev box if you installed toolkit manually. just double-check any other system packages you need. `apt remove --purge nvidia-cuda-toolkit libcudart-12-1` then `sudo ldconfig` should let /usr/local/cuda be used.

eli: did that. after removing, relogin, `ldd` now points to /usr/local/cuda/lib64. re-ran cmake/make and now hitting PTX error from ptxas: `ptxas fatal   : Value 'sm_86' is not defined for option 'gpu-name'`

rosie: that means your nvcc arch flags might be incompatible with the bundled ptxas in the toolkit. what's the target arch set in cmake (e.g., sm_75, sm_86)?

eli: build output shows `-arch=sm_86` in nvcc flags. machine is an A100 (sm_80).

samir: ok set arch to sm_80 for A100. in our repo we have CMake option `-DRUNTIME_CUDA_ARCH=80` (or `sm_80`). try `cmake .. -DRUNTIME_CUDA_ARCH=80` and rebuild.

eli: changing to 80 and rebuilding... progress! link now succeeds, runtime binary starts and unit tests for GPU pass 11/11. woohoo :tada:

jess: welcome aboard eli — awesome debugging! :sparkles: ping if you want a runthrough of the dev image and common gotchas.

eli: thanks everyone for the quick help. i'll jot down steps in my onboarding notes: remove distro cuda packages, prefer /usr/local/cuda toolkit, align CMake arch with HW, set CUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR. closing thread.
